skill.name: pr-description
skill.description: Guide for creating comprehensive PR descriptions with structure, diagrams, testing evidence, and reviewer-focused documentation.
skill.summary: Create structured pull request descriptions with context, diagrams, testing evidence, and reviewer notes.
skill.author: BfdCampos

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 20 shows an inline Markdown filename pattern, not executable Ruby or shell code. It contains placeholders for a saved PR description name and has no execution path.
SKILL.md line 21 documents a hardcoded timestamp command for optional file naming. It does not accept untrusted input, access secrets, or run automatically as part of the skill.
SKILL.md line 22 is only an example filename inside Markdown backticks. There is no command execution or dynamic interpolation behavior.
SKILL.md line 26 opens a Markdown example block for the PR template. A code fence marker is documentation formatting, not executable shell or Ruby code.
SKILL.md line 33 references the mermaid skill by name inside a template placeholder. It is a diagram instruction and does not invoke a local command or shell.
SKILL.md lines 51-55 show example test commands that a developer may document in a PR. The skill asks for evidence of commands already run; it does not execute them automatically.
SKILL.md line 55 is the closing marker for a Markdown code fence. It has no command semantics or runtime effect.
SKILL.md line 77 closes a Markdown template block. The flagged backticks are formatting syntax, not a Ruby shell execution operator.
SKILL.md line 81 mentions the mermaid skill for diagram styling inside inline Markdown. This is a documentation reference, not executable command invocation.
SKILL.md lines 133-138 contain an example testing section with common project commands. The commands are illustrative evidence for a PR description and are not run by the skill.
SKILL.md line 33 asks for a Mermaid diagram of the reviewed change. It does not direct the agent to enumerate host systems, users, network interfaces, or other reconnaissance targets.
SKILL.md line 36 asks for an entity relationship diagram when data relationships changed. This is normal PR documentation and not system reconnaissance.
SKILL.md line 79 is a section header about Mermaid diagrams. A diagram documentation heading does not request system discovery or sensitive environment inspection.

content.value_statement: Reviewers waste time when pull requests lack context, testing evidence, and diagrams. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to produce structured PR descriptions.
actual_capabilities: Provides a repeatable PR description structure with summary, goals, changes, testing, reviewer notes, and future work.
Guides the assistant to include Mermaid data flow diagrams and entity relationship diagrams when relevant.
Prompts for exact testing evidence, validation results, screenshots, and command output summaries.
Keeps PR descriptions reviewer-focused by separating context, risks, assumptions, and follow-up work.
Handles missing scope, testing, or diagrams by asking for clarification or marking placeholders for review.
limitations: It depends on the user or agent to provide accurate change details.
It cannot verify that tests passed unless evidence is supplied.
It may create placeholder diagrams when architecture details are incomplete.
It focuses on PR documentation, not merge strategy or reviewer assignment.

use_cases.title: Document a Feature Pull Request
use_cases.description: Create a complete PR description for a feature branch with goals, changes, testing, and reviewer notes.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Refactor Review
use_cases.description: Explain architectural changes with diagrams, risks, assumptions, and validation details for a focused review.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team PRs
use_cases.description: Use a consistent PR format so teams compare scope, testing, and deferred work across submissions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic PR Description
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a small change with known scope.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pr-description skill to draft a PR description for these changes: [paste summary]. Include summary, changes, testing, and reviewer notes.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Testing Evidence
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for improving an existing draft.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pr-description skill to improve my draft. Add commands run, results, validation steps, and future work from this context: [paste details].

prompt_templates.title: Document Architecture Changes
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for services, data flow, or schema changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pr-description skill to create a review-ready PR description for a service change. Include a Mermaid data flow diagram and an ERD if relationships changed.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Review Package
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for a large or high-risk pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pr-description skill to inspect the branch context I provide, separate goals from future work, flag assumptions, and produce a final PR description.

output_examples.input: Feature branch adds password reset emails and updates user settings validation.
output_examples.output: A PR description with concise context, reviewer-focused changes, testing evidence, and notes about email delivery assumptions.

output_examples.input: Refactor moves billing logic into a separate service and adds new invoice relationships.
output: Summary of the billing service split.
Data flow diagram placeholder for invoice processing.
Relationship notes for customers, invoices, and payments.
Testing section with command names, results, and manual validation.

output_examples.input: Draft PR lacks testing details and diagrams.
output_examples.output: The skill asks for completed test evidence first, then adds pending validation and diagram placeholders for reviewer confirmation.

best_practices: Provide business context, changed areas, and any known reviewer concerns before asking for the PR description.
Include exact testing evidence and validation results so the output does not overstate confidence.
Review generated diagrams and placeholders before publishing the final pull request.
anti_patterns: Do not use generic summaries that hide the reason for the change.
Do not claim tests passed unless the evidence is available.
Do not include diagrams that conflict with the actual code or data model.

faq.question: Does this skill create pull requests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It helps write the PR description content. You still create or update the pull request in your development platform.

faq.question: Can it include Mermaid diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill asks for data flow diagrams and entity relationship diagrams when they help reviewers understand the change.

faq.question: Does it run tests for me?
faq.answer: No. It asks for commands run and results, but test execution remains the responsibility of the user or agent workflow.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the change summary, important files, goals, test results, risks, screenshots, and any follow-up work.

faq.question: Can it handle incomplete context?
faq.answer: Yes. It can ask clarification questions and mark placeholders, but complete context produces more accurate PR descriptions.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
